transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because there’s been… family trouble. My husband’s sister, she’s been working things with the family business, trying to get control of the money and keep me out of decisions. People keep saying it’s nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on over a year.
Do you feel that others, like your husband or his sister, are deliberately trying to harm or deceive you in some way?

Yes… I do. Mostly his sister. She’s been working things with the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. They try to make it sound like I’m misunderstanding, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been more than a year.
Do you generally find yourself mistrusting people, even those close to you, or feeling like others are out to get you?

I don’t know about everybody. I just know what’s been happening with my husband’s sister and the family business. She’s trying to get control of the money and keep me pushed out, and people keep acting like I’m making too much of it… but I’ve seen enough. It’s been over a year.
Outside of this situation with your husband’s sister, do you often feel mistrustful or suspicious of others in your daily life?
Not really… I don’t think so. I keep to myself mostly. It’s this thing with his sister that’s been the problem.
Do you believe things about your husband’s sister’s actions that others might find hard to understand or not based on reality?

I guess they might say that. But I’m not making it up. I came here because she’s been working things with that family business, trying to get control of the money and push me out. People keep smoothing it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing… it’s been over a year.
Can you tell me specifically what you’ve seen or experienced that makes you believe your husband’s sister is trying to take control of the money and push you out of decisions?

It’s just… the way she’s been working things with the family business. Money things, decisions getting made without me, and then everyone acts like it’s nothing or tries to smooth it over. I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on more than a year.
Do you believe that no matter how much others say there’s no truth to it, you still know in your mind that your husband’s sister is trying to take control of the money and push you out?

Yes… I mean, that’s why I came. People keep telling me it’s nothing, trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. She’s been working things with the business and the money, and I feel like she’s trying to push me out. It’s been going on a long time now.
Even when people have shown you evidence that her actions weren’t meant to exclude you or take control, do you still believe deep down that she’s trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes. I know what people say, and they try to explain it away, but… I still believe she’s working things with the family business to get control of the money and leave me out of decisions. It’s been going on too long for me to think it’s nothing.

Even when people have shown you clear proof that her actions weren't meant to exclude you or take control, do you still believe deep down that she's trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes. I know they’ve shown me things and tried to say it’s not like that, but… I still know what I’ve been seeing. She’s been working the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out. It’s been more than a year.

Even when people have shown you clear proof that her actions weren't meant to exclude you or take control, do you still believe deep down that she's trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes. I know I’ve said it already, but… I still believe she’s been working things with the family business, trying to get control of the money and leave me out of decisions. People can try to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been over a year.

Even when people have shown you clear proof that her actions weren't meant to exclude you or take control, do you still believe deep down that she's trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes… I still believe it. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been more than a year now.

Even when people have shown you clear proof that her actions weren't meant to exclude you or take control, do you still believe deep down that she's trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes. I know people keep saying that’s not what she’s doing, but I don’t believe that. She’s been working things with the family business to get control of the money and push me out. I’ve seen it for over a year now.

inference_history.note: The patient's responses suggest a possible Delusional Disorder (F22) given the persistent, non-bizarre delusion focused on a specific theme (i.e., the belief that her husband's sister is scheming to take control of the family business). The exclusion of generalized mistrust or paranoia beyond this specific situation makes Schizophrenia (F30.2) less likely and reduces the likelihood of other psychotic or mood-related disorders (e.g., F43.22 and F60.3). However, the persistence of the belief despite lack of strong evidence may also indicate a Personality Disorder, specifically Paranoid Type (F60.2), though further evaluation is needed to differentiate between F22 and F60.2.

The patient's continued insistence on a specific delusional theme (persecution by husband's sister regarding family business and money) without broader symptoms of anxiety, trauma, or personality dysfunction maintains the differential diagnosis. No new disorder added or ruled out.

F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood) is ruled out as the primary concern appears to be centered on persistent mistrust and fixation on the husband's sister's intentions rather than a reaction to a psychosocial stressor with mixed anxiety and depressed mood. F22 (Persistent Delusional Disorder) remains likely given the patient's fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief about the sister's intentions despite reassurance. F60.2 (Paranoid Personality Disorder) remains a candidate due to the persistent suspicion and mistrust of a family member, though the focus appears more circumscribed than a lifelong pattern. The responses do not indicate clear evidence of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders to support F20 codes, nor do they suggest brief psychotic disorder (F23) or shared delusional disorder (F24).
